title: The dimension of a Noetherian local ring is at most the number of generators of its maximal ideal
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring and suppose $\mathfrak m$ is generated by $n$ elements $y_1,\dots,y_n$. Then the Krull dimension of $R$ (the supremum of the lengths $l$ of chains $\mathfrak q_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak q_l$ of prime ideals of $R$) satisfies $\dim R\le n$.

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00KQ (proposition-dimension, line 14521): dim R equals the minimal number d'(R) of generators of an ideal of definition; m itself is an ideal of definition generated by n elements, so dim R <= n
